ideas.arrival: built in the 2010s, about 100 years after it was imagined

ideas.profit: no lasting profit

verdict.money_why: Firms build it into what they sell, and many can make it, so no seller keeps much.

ideas.arrival: built in 2006, 95 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Hugo Gernsback
ideas.line: Converts speech or text from one human language into another automatically.
ideas.name: Language Rectifier
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Travellers, migrants and other ordinary people buy it to use themselves, firms buy it too, and once it works many can offer it, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Letting any two people talk and read across languages opens up travel, trade and work, which is worth an industry of its own.

verdict.prize_why: News sorted to each reader's interests changes how the news trade reaches people.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1960s, about 50 years after it was imagined

verdict.prize_why: Sending a copy of a written page down a wire in moments saved offices days of post and was worth an industry.

ideas.arrival: built in 2007, 96 years after it was imagined

verdict.prize_why: Seeing the person you are talking to is something most people now use, and it is worth an industry.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1960s, about 50 years after it was imagined

ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Shippers and warehouses buy it, and as it can be copied the firms that already equip warehouses collect.

ideas.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
ideas.line: A dining place where machines cook and deliver meals with no staff.

ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Restaurant operators buy the machinery, and since many could build it the catering-equipment makers with service networks collect.

ideas.author: Hugo Gernsback

verdict.prize_why: Learning during sleep would add to schooling rather than replace it, which is worth an industry but not a new way of life; unlike the knowledge-loading machines it teaches at the ordinary pace.

ideas.author: Hugo Gernsback
ideas.line: Reads what someone is thinking and prints it as written text.

ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people would get it inside gadgets they buy, and once it works it is easy to copy, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Writing by thought is a convenience, since keyboards and speech already do the job.

ideas.author: Hugo Gernsback
ideas.line: A battery-powered aircraft that ferries passengers around a city like a hired car.
ideas.name: Aerocab (Aeroflyer)
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: The carrier or fleet operator that runs the air cab buys it and charges riders, and since several firms could build it, the makers that already build and service such craft collect.
verdict.prize_why: Hired flight across a city, working as promised, would be an industry of its own beside road cabs.

ideas.author: Kenneth Brown
ideas.line: A car on two wheels that keeps itself upright using a spinning gyroscope.

ideas.profit: competed away to users

ideas.work: Two Boys in a Gyrocar the story of a New York to Paris motor race

ideas.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
ideas.line: A lift driven by strong electromagnets instead of cables.

ideas.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
